title: Wren and the Verdict
premise: When coroner Ivo Iversen receives a confession letter for a drowning ruled accidental twenty years ago—signed with her own childhood nickname, Wren—she realizes someone knows she falsified that verdict under pressure from the town's founding family. A second letter promises the surviving witness is alive and will surface only if Ivo reopens the case. As she digs, the town's powerful Aldous family closes ranks, and Ivo must choose between protecting her quiet life and exposing the truth. In the end, the witness is revealed to be the confessor himself—the now-dying patriarch who wants absolution before death—and Ivo publishes the corrected verdict, surrendering her invisibility but reclaiming her name.
about_author: Mirabel Zhou is a former small-town records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing other people's unfinished business before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about ordinary people forced to stop looking away.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On an ordinary morning of filing paperwork, two letters arrive: one confessing to the 2004 drowning of Danny Aldous, one promising 'more if you look.' The confession is signed 'Wren'—a name no living person should know. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in the comfort of routine beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She pulls Danny Aldous's file and confronts her own twenty-year-old signature on a verdict she never believed. Flashbacks reveal how Aldous patriarch Edmund pressured her at twenty-six to rule it accidental. Emotional beat: shame resurfacing, the first admission that she was complicit.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears He's Dead
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She quietly interviews Danny's old friends about the witness everyone claims died in a car crash years ago—Tommy Reeve. Each interview yields the same rehearsed grief and a warning to let it lie. Emotional beat: isolation deepening as the town's silence reveals its architecture.

chapters.title: The Widow's Tea
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Invited to tea by Edmund's daughter-in-law Celeste, Ivo is offered a generous donation to the coroner's office—a bribe dressed as gratitude. Celeste mentions 'Wren' casually, watching her face. Emotional beat: the seduction of power, and Ivo realizing she's being managed, not threatened.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Re-examining preserved evidence, she finds bruising on Danny's exhumed photos consistent with restraint, not accident—and a second set of initials on the autopsy request: T.R. Tommy Reeve signed as assisting medic. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the case was buried twice, once in water, once in ink.

chapters.title: A Third Letter
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The third letter arrives with a photograph of Ivo herself at Danny's funeral, and instructions: exhume, reopen, or the letters go to the state attorney. Someone is watching her house. Emotional beat: fear tipping into fury—she decides to stop reacting and start hunting the sender.

chapters.title: The Grave That Isn't Empty
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, shifting briefly to Edmund's. Ivo obtains a court order and exhumes the grave registered to Tommy Reeve—it holds no body, only stones and a rotted coat. Meanwhile Edmund, frail and oxygen-dependent, burns papers in his study. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into vertigo; the dead man was never buried anywhere.

chapters.title: Confession, Second Draft
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Dying, he confesses to his nurse what really happened: Danny drowned during a drunken fight, Tommy helped cover it up, then fled and has been paying Edmund's silence ever since. The letters were Edmund's own doing—he wants the truth out before he dies, using Ivo as his instrument. Emotional beat: corrupted love; a father destroying his family's name to unburden his soul.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Confronting Edmund on his deathbed, she learns why 'Wren': he knew her as a child, before she learned to disappear, and chose the name to remind her she was once brave. He gives her Tommy's location and his written confession. Emotional beat: grief and release entangled; forgiveness she didn't plan to give.

chapters.title: The Corrected Verdict
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She files the amended ruling naming Danny's true cause of death, testifies despite the town's fury, and watches Tommy Reeve—alive, gray, unremarkable—walk into the courthouse to give his statement. The last scene: Ivo signs her full name, not her title, in the register. Emotional beat: quiet resurrection; identity reclaimed at the cost of invisibility.
